author: Nicholas Ward
title: Recent Purchase: Broadcom - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO)
text:
On Thursday afternoon, Broadcom ( AVGO ) gave me a nice reprieve from all of the negative news surrounding my portfolio with what I believe to be a solid Q4. The company posted 12% growth on the top-line and 27% growth on the bottom. Free cash flow was up 47% y/y. The company returned $2.26b to shareholders ($723 in dividends and $1.53b in stock buybacks). And most importantly, management announced a 51% dividend increase. This increased pushed AVGO’s forward yield up above 4.5%. With this in mind, I decided to buy more on Friday. I added shares to my position in the morning at $236.08. Unfortunately for me, the market sold off again later in the day. Before the market closed, I decided to add again, buying more shares at $229.38.
Q4 Highlights AVGO operates 3 main segments: wired, wireless, and enterprise storage. Wired and enterprise storage posed strong Q4 numbers, while wireless lagged.
Wired segment posted $2.2b of sales in the recent quarter, accounting for 41% of the company’s overall sales. This segment, which makes up nearly one half of the company’s sales grew 3% y/y. Management did not, however, that networking and computer offload (from cloud data centers) made up over two-thirds of the company’s wired segment and this portion of the segment revenue posted 22% growth. This is on top of 10% y/y growth last year. In other words, while certain legacy areas of the wired segment are struggling, in general, this segment has a strong growth engine within it that doesn’t show any sign of stopping in a world where cloud migration is only increasing.
Enterprise storage accounted for ~23% of the company’s Q4 sales, at $1.3b. This is yet another business which benefits from the cloud shift. AVGO’s enterprise storage segment posted 96% y/y growth. This figure is bolstered by the acquisition of Brocade that the company made about a year ago, though management noted that if you stripped out the brocade sales, the enterprise segment’s organic y/y growth would still have been in the double digits. Regardless, I’m not going to penalize the company for making an acquisition that resulted in growth. While I don’t count of near triple digit growth from this segment next year, I wouldn’t be surprised to see strong double digit numbers once again.
AVGO’s wireless segment represented roughly 31% of Q4 revenues. This is a large segment for the company and it didn’t perform particularly well, down 5% y/y. Management attempted to put a positive spin on the number, saying that it was still above their expectations; however, negative 5% is negative 5% and while data center growth bolstered the company’s numbers during Q4, Broadcom is going to need to get its act together in the mobile space to keep up growth long-term.
Negative news seems to be all around us with regard to the smart phone market. Apple ( AAPL ) went from the most loved company in the world with a market cap well above $1t a month or so ago to a downright dog, down approximately 25% from the recent highs today. I’ve been a buyer on this Apple downswing, believing it to be an overreaction by the market; however, I’m no soothsayer and only time will tell whether or not there is truly significant weakness in the mobile handset space.
AVGO is a major supplier of Apple, as well as many of the other global smart phone leaders, and it will continue to suffer if we have reached “peak smart-phone”. This isn’t a pressing concern for me personally. I understand that there will become a time when some sort of new technological innovation replaces the smart phone, but I don’t see that day coming anytime soon and if/when it does, I suspect that leading semi-conductor companies like AVGO will play a role in the transition. Furthermore, recent moves by the company have diversified its business away from the mobile space a bit. In Q4, the data center piece was the biggest highlight. This is a strong growth industry that all semi-conductor companies are trying to take market share in.
Full Year Numbers and Forward Guidance Thankfully, the recent negative wireless declines haven’t become a trend yet. On the contrary, wireless was actually AVGO’s strongest segment on the full-year, posting 20% growth. This strong growth helped to fuel total annual revenue growth of 18% for FY18. EPS growth on the year was equally impressive, up ~30% on a non-GAAP basis.
AVGO’s GAAP and non-GAAP EPS figures came in at $28.44 and $20.82, respectively. This means that at the current share price of ~ $230, shares are trading at near-single digit multiples.
Furthermore, management remains confident in continued growth. Specifically related to the wireless segment, management says that it expects to make up for recent market share losses in the current generations of phones by re-taking share in the second half of FY19 in upcoming generations.
In the software space, forward guidance was all focused on profits. AVGO management is known for demanding high margins and cutting fat when it takes over businesses. It appears that this isn’t going to change with the newly acquired CA Technologies. CEO Hock Tan highlighted the fact that CA’s prior business model was wasteful with regard to focusing on landing accounts and taking broader market share. He said that the company should have been focusing on the largest 500 accounts or so, which make up ~70% of the software sales. Moving forward, AVGO will be more intensely focused on these large accounts, providing them with the services they require, rather than trying to land new accounts at all costs. This transition should result in the generation~$2.5b in operational profits annually from the CA platforms.
For FY19, management expects to see ~$24.5b in revenues and operating margins of ~51%. This represents solid double digit revenue growth expectations over the ~$21b of sales that AVGO produced in FY18. Once the restructuring of the CA assets is completed, that margin is expected to rise. Management targets 55% in 2020.
Shareholder Returns What really inspired my recent purchases was management’s dedication towards shareholder returns. The company remains committed to returning ~50% of free cash flows to shareholders in the form of a dividend. AVGO generated ~$8.2b of free cash flow in 2018 and therefore, it increased its recent dividend to ~$4b. The new quarterly dividend is $2.65/share (representing 51% y/y growth).
AVGO has been known for very large dividend growth in recent years. The company’s last three dividend increases were 100%, 71%, and 51%. Obviously I don’t expect to see these types of increases continue over the long-term, though I do think that AVGO can realistically continue to provide double digit increases over the short-medium term. Considering that the company’s forward yield is above 4.5% after the recent increase, this makes this a pretty unique DGI company with regard to its combination of high yield and high dividend growth potential.
Adding to the generous shareholder returns, AVGO CFO Tom Krause mentioned that the company currently has plans to return ~$8b to shareholders in FY19 in the form of share buybacks. This represents the other ~50% of free cash flow that isn’t being dedicated to the dividend combined with the $4.3b of cash that currently sits on the balance sheet.
Honestly, I was a bit surprised to see such aggressive shareholder return metrics being discussed. While I’m typically a fan of share buybacks, I wouldn’t mind seeing AVGO management use some of the expected free cash flows/cash no the balance sheet to pay down the ~$17.5b of debt that current sits on the balance sheet. I don’t think that AVGO is over burdened with debt at the moment, but management did say that it hoped to continue M&A in the software space and if this is true, I’d like to see them being proactive with balance sheet management.
Conclusion This is the risk of an investment in AVGO. This management team is known for being aggressive. The company is oftentimes considered to be a “roll-up” type company with regard to its regular M&A (having to buy growth). Thus far, the model is working well. I’m obviously willing to trust the management team as a shareholder, though I admit that sometimes these situations look great…until they don’t.
Maybe I’m whistling past the graveyard here, but even so, I’m very happy to collect this ~4.5% yield and I look forward to the dividend growth announcement this time next year. AVGO hasn’t disappointed me thus far and I have to reason to believe that it will in the near-term. I think the stock looks cheap (especially if management is able to hit its guidance numbers). Right now, AVGO makes up ~2.2% of my portfolio. It is now a top-10 position for me. I don’t have any plans to bump it into the top 5, but I am overweight the name and don’t plan on selling shares unless we see a significant move to the upside.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AVGO, AAPL.
